How to quote this pack

Send back one row per line

Complete the response table at the back of this pack (or the same columns in your own sheet). Add rows where you offer an alternative. Attach the specification sheet, the electrical load sheet and a photograph or brochure for every powered item. Quote in USD FOB and state the port.

Every quotation must state

  • Brand and model per line — premium commercial-grade equipment, not entry-level or domestic.
  • Unit price and quantity in USD FOB, line total, and volume discount tiers from 2 units upward.
  • Electrical detail — rated kW, voltage, phase, frequency and the breaker size the unit needs. Every powered item.
  • Dimensions and weight per item, packed and unpacked, for shipping volume and site planning.
  • Certifications — CE with test report, ISO 9001, food-grade material certificates, enclosed. For electrical goods, the South African NRCS letter of authority status and the SANS/IEC 60335 test report — CE alone is supporting evidence, not a substitute for the LoA.
  • Nameplate and drawing — a photograph of the rating plate and a dimensioned drawing to ±5 mm for every powered line. A brochure photograph is not a drawing.
  • MOQ, lead time, packing — production time to FOB, export documentation, and whether you consolidate a mixed container.
  • South African import support — 400 V / 50 Hz, three-phase plus neutral and earth, IEC 60309 (Commando) plug or gland tails — not a Chinese or Australian plug. State the HS code and whether you will quote CIF Durban as well as FOB.
  • Payment terms — deposit percentage and balance terms (T/T), and whether you accept a letter of credit.
  • After-sales — spare-parts list with part numbers, remote commissioning support, warranty period.

Automatic rejects — do not quote around these

  • Bronze dies only on the extruder (A1/A3). A Teflon die is rejected without negotiation.
  • Low-temperature drying only (A4), 40–45 °C at 55–65% humidity over 12–24 hours. A high-temperature fast dryer breaks the product story.
  • Dried-pasta cook cycle, 8–12 minutes (B1). A fresh-pasta or rapid-cook cooker is rejected.
  • Induction that sears (B2). A bowl that will not reach 165 °C from cold in 90 seconds, or a flat hob with a trivet under the wok, is rejected.
  • Dual-tank, non-carbonated slush (F1). Carbonated machines are rejected.

Commercial conditions and site

Validity — 30 days minimum, ex-VAT. Delivery and installation quoted as separate line items.

Payment — 50% deposit on award, balance on delivery; large items may be staged. State your terms.

Award — we reserve the right to split the award by zone or category.

Target — quotes returned within 10 working days.

Store — ~42 m² mall inline unit; 900 mm counters; 1.2 m minimum aisles.

Power — 400 V three-phase, 50 Hz, 60 A distribution board in the kitchen zone.

No gas — extraction canopy over the hot line only, 1.5 m, ≥ 1,500 CFM, baffle filters, ducted to the mall riser.

Water — filtration and softening ahead of the cooker and wash-down; grease trap on the waste line.

Delivery — mall-managed site, booked windows, no on-site storage; quote cartage accordingly.

What changed in version 2.0

The wok is now a specified machine, not a category

B2 is written as an induction automatic wok with a measurable heat floor, a magnetic bowl, programmable cycles and a throughput test — because “automatic stir-fry machine” covers everything from a real wok to a heated bowl with a lid. The 304 bowl in the September pack was wrong: 304 is non-magnetic and will not couple to an induction coil, so the line now asks for carbon steel or magnetic 430/clad. Suppliers answer the heat question with a number and a test method. The quantity is now resolved: three units at 8 kW is the most the 60 A board carries, and the pack also asks for a four-unit 5 kW alternative to price against it.

Every line now has a photograph and an image slot

Each card carries a reference image of the machine class. Where we have no honest photograph the card carries an empty frame for the supplier's own model — an image of the machine they are actually offering is part of the quotation, not a nice-to-have.

Two lines still carry an open decision

B2 quantity — two or four woks. The tier price decides. E4 — collectibles shelving versus grab-and-go sightline; quote both and we choose on price.

The induction automatic wok

Line B2 is the machine this pack is built around. It replaces the static hob that made finish-to-order too slow, and it is why sauces no longer have to be held. The store is all-electric in a mall, so gas is off the table — the burden of proof is on the induction unit to sear, not warm.

Reference image — indicative. Replace with the offered model.
B2

Induction automatic wok — open-bowl auto stir-fry station

QTY 3 (price 3 × 8 kW and 4 × 5 kW) POWER 8 kW each · 400 V 3φ

Ricardo's specified machine: induction, automatic. Set into the pass, bowl visible to the customer line.

Heavy-duty commercial induction automatic wok with a motorised open bowl and programmable cooking cycles, set into the pass at 950 mm so sauce and pasta are tossed in full view of the queue. Quote three units at 8 kW, which is the most a 60 A board carries, and price a four-unit 5 kW alternative for comparison. This is the machine that makes finish-to-order affordable: on a static hob, sauces get held that should never be held. It must sear and reduce, not warm — and the bowl must stay on its coil while it works, so an open bowl that lifts off to toss is not acceptable.

Desired specifications
  • Induction, 400 V three-phase, 50 Hz, 8 kW continuous per unit (not peak). State nameplate kW — a photograph of the nameplate is required with the quote
  • Bowl surface 165 °C from cold in under 90 seconds, measured at the bowl base; recovery to temperature within 60 seconds after a 1 kg load. State the test method
  • Bowl: seamless spun carbon steel or magnetic 430 / clad stainless, 3.0–4.0 mm, Ø 350–400 mm, 5–8 L usable. 304 alone is non-magnetic and will not couple to the coil — do not offer it
  • Concave induction coil matched to the bowl radius, full coverage. A flat hob with a trivet under the wok is rejected
  • Motorised rotation or auto-toss, 10–40 rpm variable, bowl seated on the coil throughout; manual tilt and manual toss override for the cook
  • Programmable recipe cycles — power level, rotation speed, time — with at least 20 stored recipes, batch timer, audible alarm and a temperature log export
  • Throughput at least 45 portions per hour per unit on a 140 g dried-pasta plus 180 g sauce finish; state cycle time and test conditions
  • Open bowl, visible from the customer side, splash guard to the queue; brushed 304 body; stated noise level at 1 m
  • Over-temperature cut-out, dry-burn and no-load protection, rotation interlock, emergency stop, IPX4
  • State smoke and fume generation and the canopy airflow you require per unit; unit must fit under a 1.5 m hood at 950 mm pass height
  • CE with test report, SANS/IEC 60335-2-9 alignment, NRCS letter of authority support; English manual, wiring diagram, spare-parts list, 2-year commercial warranty
Automatic reject: Gas; flat hob with trivet; 304-only bowl; < 6 kW continuous; timer-only control with no temperature feedback; bowl that lifts off the coil
Where to quote: Guangdong Qinxin / Lestov — rotating heavy-duty wok, US$2,158–2,259 FOB · Dongguan Jingcheng — auto cooking robot, US$1,999 FOB · Hengtiantai — 5 kW intelligent stir-fry, electromagnetic · Qihao — intelligent multifunctional stir-fry, electromagnetic · Category search — electric stir-fry machines

Factory acceptance test — run it before you ship

  • Cold start to 280 °C pan-surface temperature in under three minutes, measured with a contact probe at the bowl base.
  • Three consecutive 3 kg batches tossed at full rotation without spill or stall, with the bowl at temperature throughout.
  • Twenty consecutive finish cycles with no power derate and no control fault.
  • Full cook of one portion in under three minutes, filmed, with the cycle program and the wattage shown on the panel.
  • Ship only against a signed test sheet and the video.

What "automatic" must mean on this line

A rotating bowl and a timer is not automatic. The machine must run a stored recipe cycle — power level, rotation speed and time — that a cook selects with one touch, and it must hold that cycle repeatably across a service. Manual override stays available, because the pass is a show station and the cook still finishes by eye. If the only control is a dial and a switch, it is a heated mixer, not an automatic wok.

A1

Pasta extruder — bronze die (Pasta Theatre)

QTY 1 POWER 230 V · ~0.6 kW

Replaces the legacy Gustotek GUSGT108 reference.

Commercial single-head pasta extruder for in-store production, built into the customer-facing line as the Pasta Theatre. It extrudes the Golden Blend dough; the output is dried in store (A4) and later cooked as dried pasta (B1). Bronze die head is mandatory: the rough, sauce-gripping surface is the texture promise, and a Teflon die is rejected without negotiation.

Desired specifications
  • Extrusion capacity 12–15 kg/hr at 12% moisture, small footprint (counter or stand mount). 5 kg/hr starves peak service — state your output at 12% moisture
  • Bronze die head — Teflon die is an automatic reject
  • Food-grade stainless body (304 or better), CE certified, English manual
  • Glass or acrylic surround so extrusion is fully visible to the customer line
  • 230 V single phase; stated rated kW and breaker size
  • Tool-free strip-down for cleaning; spare die set and auger available as priced spares
  • State die-change time and the shapes the standard head supports
Automatic reject: Teflon die
Where to quote: Zhengzhou Maosu — small-footprint extruder · Screwbarrelchina — Italian pasta / macaroni line

In-store pasta drying cabinet — low temperature, humidity controlled

QTY 1 POWER 230 V · ~2.5 kW

Compact in-store low-temperature drying cabinet sitting with the extruder in the Pasta Theatre: the bridge between watching pasta being made and eating it. B1

Commercial pasta cooker — 9-basket, electric

QTY 1 POWER ~6 kW

Ricardo's #1 priority machine. Sized against ~120 dishes/hour at peak.

Electric thermostatic commercial pasta cooker with basket lifters and timer, nine baskets, in GN format. It cooks dried pasta in 8–12 minutes and holds al dente without overcooking; the clean-draining baskets feed the wok finish. Nine baskets is the service-line specification — at four woks this cooker is the binding station at roughly 162 covers an hour. A fresh-pasta or rapid-cook (60–180 s) cooker is an automatic reject: this store cooks dried pasta.

Desired specifications
  • Electric, thermostatic, 9 baskets, GN pan format — quote 9; state if 6 is your only size
  • 8–12 minute dried-pasta cook cycle, batch-to-order basket lift with timer
  • Water top-up / auto-level, drain valve, 304 stainless body
  • Throughput to support ~120 dishes/hour at peak alongside the woks — state baskets/hour
  • 230 V single or 400 V three-phase — state required supply, rated kW and breaker
  • No gas; no fresh-pasta / rapid-cook cooker (automatic reject)
  • State water connection, drain size and footprint
Automatic reject: Gas or rapid-cook

Read this before you quote a bigger wok

The board is 60 A three-phase at 400 V — about 41.6 kW at nameplate. Three 8 kW woks is the most it carries, and only on normal kitchen diversity: the cooker and the dishwasher must not peak with a full wok line. Four 8 kW woks is a board upgrade to 80–100 A, not a diversity argument. If your unit draws more than 8 kW, say so on the line — a 12 kW wok changes what the store has to install. The final board, diversity and cable sizing are signed off by the electrical engineer, not by this table.

What this pack does not cover

The central kitchen is a separate pack

This document is the retail store kit only. The central kitchen (commissary) is a different build with different suppliers and its own electrical design: spiral blast freezer, freeze dryer, jacketed cooking kettles, the pasta production and drying line, MAP tray sealing and the can fill-and-seam line. Mixing the two into one request makes every quote uncomparable, so it ships as pack two.

Fit-out, not equipment

Shopfront, joinery, counters, the extraction canopy, floor and wall finishes, and the electrical installation itself are the fit-out contract, not this pack. Suppliers quoting here quote equipment and, where offered, commissioning.

By others — say so if your quote assumes any of this

  • Extraction canopy, ducting to the mall riser, odour control and make-up air — fit-out contract. Every hot-line supplier must still state the airflow its machine needs.
  • Air-conditioning and kitchen cooling for roughly 47 kW of connected load in 42 m².
  • Floor gully, mop sink, instant hot water and water filtration.
  • Electrical installation, distribution board, cable and containment — by the electrical contractor, signed off by a registered person.
  • Ice machine, kitchen display screen (KDS) and the POS software licence.
  • Shopfront, joinery, counters, wall and floor finishes, signage.

What we need back first

B2 and B1 — the wok and the cooker — because they set the board, the hood and the line length. Then A1 and A4, the extruder and the drying cabinet, because they set the theatre footprint. Everything else is off-the-shelf and can follow once the line is fixed.
